facts.text: A manufacturer of heavy off-road machines for construction, mining and quarrying already sells a system that warns the operator when the machine gets too close to an object.
facts.quote: already sells a system that warns the operator when the machine gets too close to an object.

facts.text: The heavy off-road machine manufacturer is developing a system that automatically applies the brakes if the operator does not react.
facts.quote: It is now developing a system that also applies the brakes automatically if the operator does not react.

facts.text: Prototype hardware and software for the heavy off-road automatic braking system arrive in mid-2027.
facts.quote: Prototype hardware and software arrive in mid-2027

facts.text: Validation of the heavy off-road automatic braking system must finish in under four months after prototype hardware and software arrive in mid-2027.
facts.quote: Prototype hardware and software arrive in mid-2027, and validation must then finish in under four months

facts.text: Past validation of comparable heavy off-road machine functions took three to four years of physical testing and tuning per machine model.
facts.quote: past validation of comparable functions took three to four years of physical testing and tuning per machine model.

facts.text: The heavy off-road automatic braking system must work across more than 100 job-site types.

facts.text: The heavy off-road automatic braking system must work across more than 10 operating scenarios per machine.
facts.quote: more than 10 operating scenarios per machine

facts.text: The heavy off-road automatic braking system must work in many weather and light conditions.

facts.text: The heavy off-road automatic braking system must work across many machine models with different sizes and sensor positions.

facts.text: The machine types and brake systems for the heavy off-road automatic braking system are not yet confirmed.
facts.quote: the machine types and brake systems are not yet confirmed

facts.text: Because machine types and brake systems were not yet confirmed, the braking research covered wheeled, tracked and articulated machines.
facts.quote: Because the machine types and brake systems are not yet confirmed, the research covered wheeled, tracked and articulated machines.

facts.text: The braking research sought published data on differences between heavy off-road machines and road vehicles, considering mass, changing payload, slopes, loose or wet ground, wheels versus tracks, articulated steering, hydrostatic drives and brake-system delays.
facts.quote: considering mass, changing payload, slopes, loose or wet ground, wheels versus tracks, articulated steering, hydrostatic drives and brake-system delays, with published data.

facts.text: The braking research sought to determine the machine and brake model fidelity needed to predict stopping distance and stability with useful accuracy, comparing simple equations through multi-body and soil models for accuracy and effort.
facts.quote: Which level of machine and brake model is needed to predict stopping distance and stability with useful accuracy, comparing options from simple equations to multi-body and soil models with their accuracy and effort.

facts.text: The braking research sought to determine how machine and brake models are built and checked against real machines, including which physical tests are needed and how many.
facts.quote: How such models are built and checked against real machines, which physical tests are needed, and how many.

facts.text: The braking research sought to examine warning and braking decision logic using time to collision, stopping-distance models and risk zones, including threshold tuning for on-road vehicles and differences at off-road working speeds.
facts.quote: Which logic decides when to warn and when to brake (time to collision, stopping-distance models, risk zones), how those thresholds are tuned for on-road vehicles, and what differs at off-road working speeds.

facts.text: The braking research sought to examine staged interventions comprising warning, slowing, partial braking, full stop and preventing movement from standstill.
facts.quote: Which staged interventions are used: warning, slowing, partial braking, full stop, and preventing movement from standstill.

facts.text: The braking research sought to identify hazards caused by the braking intervention itself.
facts.quote: Which hazards the intervention itself can cause

facts.text: The braking research sought to determine how deceleration limits are set.
facts.quote: how limits on deceleration are set.

facts.text: The braking research sought to determine how a system recognizes that the operator is already reacting so that unnecessary braking is avoided.
facts.quote: How a system recognizes that the operator is already reacting, so that it does not brake without need.

facts.text: The braking research sought examples and results of simulation used to tune warning and braking thresholds before field testing.
facts.quote: How simulation has been used to tune these thresholds before field testing, with examples and results.

facts.text: The braking research was required to remain neutral across vendors, products and technologies and cover commercial, open-source, academic and in-house options.
facts.quote: The research was to stay neutral across vendors, products and technologies, and to cover commercial, open-source, academic and in-house options.

facts.text: Every important claim in the braking research was to be labeled by evidence type: independent study, standard or third-party test; a vendor's own claim; or expert opinion.
facts.quote: Each important claim was to be labeled by evidence type (independent study, standard or third-party test; a vendor's own claim; or expert opinion)

facts.text: Every source in the braking research was to be dated.
facts.quote: each source dated

facts.text: The braking research was required to report failures and limits alongside successes.
facts.quote: failures and limits reported alongside successes.

facts.text: The braking research was required to flag findings proven only for on-road vehicles as on-road evidence.
facts.quote: Findings proven only for on-road vehicles were to be flagged as such

facts.text: When information could not be found, the braking research was required to write "not found" rather than guess numbers, prices or timelines.
